title: Ibn Battuta: The road to Mecca and the first hajj, 1325–26
summary: A young judge from Tangier rides the coast road to Alexandria and up the Nile, is turned back at the Red Sea, and goes round by Gaza, Jerusalem and Damascus to make his first pilgrimage with the Syrian caravan.

events.label: A marriage on the road
events.text: At Sfax he contracted to marry the daughter of a syndic of Tunis, and she was brought to him at Tripoli. A quarrel with her father ended it before Egypt; he married the daughter of a student from Fez instead, and held the caravan a day for the wedding feast.

events.label: Alexandria: a holy man's prophecy
events.text: Burhan al-Din the Lame, an ascetic he stayed three days with, told him he would visit his brothers Farid al-Din in India, Rukn al-Din in Sind and Burhan al-Din in China. The idea had not crossed his mind, he says, and he went on until he had met all three.

events.label: Aydhab: the crossing shut
events.text: He meant to cross the Red Sea from Aydhab, but the sultan of the Beja was at war with the Mamluks and had sunk the ships. He sold his provisions, went back down the Nile to Cairo and took the long way round by Syria.

events.label: Damascus in Ramadan
events.text: He reached Damascus on 9 August 1326 and stayed through Ramadan before the pilgrim caravan left south for Medina and Mecca.
